Prealgebra · Lesson 8.2

Estimating Irrational Roots

Solve this lesson →All lessons

In 8.1 every radicand was a perfect square. Now suppose a tile setter needs a square panel covering exactly 5050 square inches. The side is 5050​, an irrational number whose decimal never ends or repeats, so we estimate it instead.

Fun fact
The Pythagoreans believed every length was a fraction. When someone proved 22​ cannot be written as any fraction, legend says the discoverer was thrown overboard for shattering that belief.
Problem
A square patch covers 5454 sq m, so the side is 5454​. Since 72=4972=49 and 82=6482=64, the root lies between 77 and 88. What is the largest whole number less than 5454​?
Show a hint
  • Look for the two perfect squares that sandwich 5454. Which perfect square sits just below 5454, and which sits just above?
  • You found that 49<54<6449<54<64. The roots keep that same order, so 7<54<87<54​<8. The floor is the smaller of those two whole numbers.
Show the full solution
Since 72=4972=49 and 82=6482=64, we have 49<54<6449<54<64, so 7<54<87<54​<8. The largest whole number below the side length is 77​. A bigger number always has a bigger square root, so trapping 5454 between two perfect squares traps the root between the two whole numbers.
Problem
A square solar farm covers 68006800 sq m. Given 822=6724822=6724 and 832=6889832=6889, what is the largest whole number of meters less than 68006800​?
Show a hint
  • You want two perfect squares with 68006800 caught between them, and you are already handed the candidates. Since 822=6724822=6724 and 832=6889832=6889, which two consecutive whole numbers do those squares belong to?
  • From 6724≤6800≤68896724≤6800≤6889 you can read off 82<6800<8382<6800​<83. The largest whole number that stays below 68006800​ is the smaller of those two bounds.
Show the full solution
From 822=6724822=6724 and 832=6889832=6889 we get 6724<6800<68896724<6800<6889. Taking roots keeps that order, so 82<6800<8382<6800​<83 and the largest whole number below the side is 8282​. The numbers are bigger but the method is the same, since the two perfect squares around the radicand are all you ever need.
Key idea
Bracketing a root. When the number under the radical is not a perfect square, its root is irrational. Its decimal goes on forever without ending or repeating, so there is no exact decimal to write down. You can still locate the root with the order rule. For numbers zero or bigger, a larger number always has a larger square root, so a>ba​>b​ exactly when a>ba>b. That lets you compare roots using exact whole-number arithmetic on the numbers inside them. Find consecutive whole numbers with m2≤n<(m+1)2m2≤n<(m+1)2. Then nn​ lies between mm and m+1m+1. The smaller one, mm, is the largest whole number below the root, called its floor. So 5454​ is between 77 and 88, since 49≤54<6449≤54<64, and its floor is 77.
Problem
A skylight has area 8383 sq in. The edge 8383​ is between 99 and 1010. The halfway square is 9.52=90.259.52=90.25. To the nearest inch, what is 8383​?
Show a hint
  • The two candidates are 99 and 1010, and the halfway point between them is 9.59.5. Whichever side of 9.59.5 the root falls on is the side you round toward.
  • Square the halfway point instead of the root, since squaring keeps the order for nonnegative numbers. The boundary is 9.52=90.259.52=90.25. Because 83<90.2583<90.25, the root is less than 9.59.5, so it rounds down.
Show the full solution
The halfway point between 99 and 1010 is 9.59.5, and 9.52=90.259.52=90.25. Since 83<90.2583<90.25, the root is below 9.59.5, so it rounds down. To the nearest inch, 83≈983​≈9​. Squaring the midpoint is the whole trick, since it turns a question about an endless decimal into one comparison of plain numbers.
Problem
A skylight has area 2121 sq in. The edge 2121​ is between 44 and 55. The halfway square is 4.52=20.254.52=20.25. To the nearest inch, what is 2121​?
Show a hint
  • The halfway point between 4 and 5 is 4.5. A root rounds up exactly when it is bigger than 4.5, which happens exactly when the number under the root is bigger than 4.524.52.
  • Compare 2121 to 4.52=20.254.52=20.25. Since 2121 is larger, 2121​ is larger than 4.54.5, so it has already passed the halfway mark.
Show the full solution
The midpoint between 44 and 55 is 4.54.5, and 4.52=20.254.52=20.25. Since 21>20.2521>20.25, the root is past 4.54.5, so it rounds up. To the nearest inch, 21≈521​≈5​. Rounding down to 44 is the usual slip here, because 2121 looks close to 1616. The midpoint square settles it instead of eyeballing.
Problem
A pendulum is 2323​ ft long. The root is between 4.74.7 and 4.84.8. Does it pass the halfway square 4.752=22.56254.752=22.5625? To the nearest tenth, what is 2323​?
Show a hint
  • The halfway mark between 4.74.7 and 4.84.8 is 4.754.75. Whichever side of 4.7524.752 the number 2323 falls on tells you which tenth the root is nearer to.
  • Compare exactly with whole numbers. Multiply both sides by 1000010000, so 4.7524.752 becomes 4752=225,6254752=225,625, while 2323 becomes 230,000230,000. Since 230,000230,000 is bigger, 2323 sits above 4.7524.752, so the root is on the higher side.
Show the full solution
The midpoint between 4.74.7 and 4.84.8 is 4.754.75, and 4.752=22.56254.752=22.5625. Since 23>22.562523>22.5625, the root is past the midpoint and rounds up. To the nearest tenth, 23=4.823​=4.8​. If the long decimal feels shaky, scale by 10,00010,000 and compare 4752=225,6254752=225,625 with 230,000230,000, which is exact whole-number work.
Problem
A drone hovers at 4141​ m. The root is between 6.46.4 and 6.56.5. Does it pass the halfway square 6.452=41.60256.452=41.6025? To the nearest tenth, what is 4141​?
Show a hint
  • You already know the root is between 6.46.4 and 6.56.5. The only question is which tenth it rounds to, so the tiebreaker is the halfway point 6.456.45.
  • Compare 4141 with 6.4526.452. To keep it exact, square 645645 and compare it to 41×10,00041×10,000. If 4141 comes out smaller, the root is below 6.456.45 and rounds down.
Show the full solution
The midpoint between 6.46.4 and 6.56.5 is 6.456.45. Comparing exactly, 6452=416,0256452=416,025 while 41×10,000=410,00041×10,000=410,000, so 41<6.45241<6.452 and 41<6.4541​<6.45. The root sits below the midpoint, so it rounds down and 41≈6.441​≈6.4​. Scaling both sides by 10,00010,000 keeps every comparison in whole numbers, so no rounding error can creep in.
Key idea
Rounding a root. To round nn​ to the nearest whole number, compare it to the halfway point between the two integers it lies between. Square that halfway value m.5m.5 and compare the result to nn. If n>(m.5)2n>(m.5)2 the root rounds up, otherwise it rounds down. Every step is exact whole-number arithmetic, so no decimal for the root is needed. The same method rounds to the nearest tenth. Square the halfway tenth and compare.
Problem
How many whole numbers nn satisfy 7<n<117<n​<11? Square the bounds, so nn must satisfy 49<n<12149<n<121. Count the whole numbers strictly between 4949 and 121121.
Show a hint
  • Squaring is fair on both sides because for nonnegative numbers a bigger value always has a bigger square root, so the order never flips. From n>7n​>7 you get n>49n>49, and from n<11n​<11 you get n<121n<121.
  • Now nn is a whole number with 49<n<12149<n<121. Both ends are strict, so 4949 and 121121 themselves are out, since their roots are exactly 77 and 1111, not between. The list runs from 5050 up through 120120. To count a solid run of whole numbers, take last minus first plus one.
Show the full solution
Squaring both bounds turns 7<n<117<n​<11 into 49<n<12149<n<121, so nn runs from 5050 through 120120. That is 120−50+1=71120−50+1=71​ whole numbers. Both ends drop out because 49=749​=7 and 121=11121​=11 exactly, and the inequalities are strict.
Problem
How many whole numbers kk satisfy 130<k<320130​<k<320​? The smallest valid kk is 1212 and the largest is 1717. Count them.
Show a hint
  • A whole number kk fits when its square lands strictly above 130130 and strictly below 320320. Find the smallest such kk and the largest such kk by checking squares.
  • The smallest fit is 1212 because 122=144>130122=144>130 while 112=121112=121 is too small. The largest fit is 1717 because 172=289<320172=289<320 while 182=324182=324 is too big. Now count from 1212 through 1717, and remember to include both ends.
Show the full solution
A whole number kk fits exactly when 130<k2<320130<k2<320. Since 112=121112=121 is too small and 122=144122=144 works, the smallest is 1212. Since 172=289172=289 works and 182=324182=324 is too big, the largest is 1717. Counting 1212 through 1717 gives 17−12+1=617−12+1=6​. Squaring kk instead of estimating the two roots keeps the whole problem in exact arithmetic.
Key idea
Counting whole numbers between two roots. Square both ends and work with the numbers under the radicals. Squaring keeps the order for nonnegative numbers, so the whole numbers kk with a<k<ba​<k<b​ are exactly the ones whose squares fall strictly between aa and bb. Bracket each end, then read off the smallest whole number above the lower root and the largest below the upper root. Count them with last minus first plus one. Check the endpoints first, since a strict inequality excludes them and a non-strict one includes them.
Problem
Cable A is 6767​ m, Cable B is 415415​ m. Square each to compare. Option 1 is Cable A, Option 2 is Cable B. Which is longer?
Show a hint
  • Comparing the radicals head on is hard, but squaring clears the roots away. Square each length using (ab)2=a2×b(ab​)2=a2×b, which leaves you two whole numbers, then compare those.
  • Cable A squared is 62×7=36×7=25262×7=36×7=252. Cable B squared is 42×15=16×15=24042×15=16×15=240. Since both cables are positive, the one with the larger square is the longer cable.
Show the full solution
Square each length. Cable A gives (67)2=62×7=252(67​)2=62×7=252, and Cable B gives (415)2=42×15=240(415​)2=42×15=240. Since 252>240252>240 and both lengths are positive, Cable A is longer, option 11​. The number out front squares too, which is the step people skip when they try to compare 6767​ and 415415​ by eye.
Problem
Evaluate (6)4(6​)4. Group the four factors into two pairs. Each pair 6×6=66​×6​=6. What is the result?
Show a hint
  • A square root undoes a square. Multiply two copies of the same root together, 6×66​×6​, and you are left with just the inside, 66. No decimals needed.
  • The fourth power is two of those pairs side by side, so (6)4=(6×6)×(6×6)=6×6(6​)4=(6​×6​)×(6​×6​)=6×6. Now just multiply those two sixes.
Show the full solution
Pair the factors. Each pair gives (6)2=6(6​)2=6, so (6)4=62=36(6​)4=62=36​. Any even power of a root collapses this way, since the copies pair off and each pair leaves just the number underneath.
Key idea
Squaring clears the radical. Two nonnegative quantities keep their order when you square them, so to compare two root expressions, square both and rank the whole numbers you get. A coefficient out front squares too, so 6767​ squares to 62×7=25262×7=252. Squaring also evaluates even powers of a root. Since a⋅a=aa​⋅a​=a, an even power splits into pairs that each reduce to the number inside, giving (a)2k=ak(a​)2k=ak. Either way you are left with a whole number and never need a decimal approximation.
Problem
A hiker covers two trails, 1818​ miles then 3333​ miles. What is the largest whole number less than 18+3318​+33​?
Show a hint
  • Bracket each root by itself first. Since 42=1642=16 and 52=2552=25, 1818​ sits between 4 and 5. Since 52=2552=25 and 62=3662=36, 3333​ sits between 5 and 6. That only tells you the sum is between 9 and 11, which is too wide to name a single floor.
  • Push the lower edge up with tenths. Check 4.22=17.644.22=17.64, which is below 18, so 18>4.218​>4.2. Check 5.72=32.495.72=32.49, which is below 33, so 33>5.733​>5.7. Adding the safe lower edges gives more than 4.2+5.74.2+5.7. Now find a matching upper edge to trap the sum between two neighbors.
Show the full solution
Sharpen each root to tenths. Since 4.22=17.64<184.22=17.64<18, we know 18>4.218​>4.2, and since 5.72=32.49<335.72=32.49<33, we know 33>5.733​>5.7, so the sum is more than 4.2+5.7=9.94.2+5.7=9.9. Going the other way, 4.252=18.0625>184.252=18.0625>18 and 5.752=33.0625>335.752=33.0625>33 make the sum less than 4.25+5.75=104.25+5.75=10. The total is caught in 9.9<18+33<109.9<18​+33​<10, so the largest whole number below it is 99​. Whole-number brackets alone only narrow the sum to between 99 and 1111, which is why the tenths are needed.
Problem
A drone flies 4040​ mi north then 7575​ mi east. The total is between 1414 and 1616. Does 40+7540​+75​ exceed 1515? What is the largest whole number below the total?
Show a hint
  • The whole question is whether the sum slips below 15 or not. Rewrite the test 40+75<1540​+75​<15 by moving one root across, so you are asking whether 40<15−7540​<15−75​. Both sides are nonnegative, since 75<9<1575​<9<15, so you are allowed to square both sides without flipping the comparison.
  • Squaring 40<15−7540​<15−75​ gives 40<225−3075+7540<225−3075​+75, which tidies up to 3075<2603075​<260. There is still one root left, so square one more time to land on plain whole numbers. Compare 302⋅75302⋅75 against 26022602.
Show the full solution
The sum already beats 1414, since 40>640​>6 and 75>875​>8. So the real test is 1515. Ask whether 40<15−7540​<15−75​, which is safe to square because 75<975​<9 keeps both sides positive. Squaring gives 40<300−307540<300−3075​, which rearranges to 3075<2603075​<260. Square again and compare 302⋅75=67,500302⋅75=67,500 with 2602=67,6002602=67,600. Since 67,500<67,60067,500<67,600, the sum really is under 1515, so it sits between 1414 and 1515 and the answer is 1414​. Every squaring step reverses cleanly here because both sides stay nonnegative throughout.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A square sticker covers 3434 sq cm. Since 52=2552=25 and 62=3662=36, the side 3434​ is between 55 and 66. What is the largest whole number less than 3434​?
Show the solution
Since 52=2552=25 and 62=3662=36, we have 25<34<3625<34<36, so 5<34<65<34​<6. The largest whole number less than 3434​ is 55​. Taking roots keeps the order, so bracketing 3434 between perfect squares brackets the root between whole numbers.
Practice
Rope 1 is 6363​ m and Rope 2 is 5757​ m. Both lie between 77 and 88. Use the order rule to decide. Option 1 is 6363​, Option 2 is 5757​. Which is longer?
Show the solution
Squaring each length gives 6363 and 5757. Since 63>5763>57, we get 63>5763​>57​, so Rope 1 is longer, option 11​. Both roots have floor 77, so the floors tie and only the numbers under the radicals tell them apart.
Practice
A square window has area 7575 sq in. The edge 7575​ is between 88 and 99. The halfway square is 8.52=72.258.52=72.25. To the nearest inch, what is 7575​?
Show the solution
The midpoint between 88 and 99 is 8.58.5, and 8.52=72.258.52=72.25. Since 75>72.2575>72.25, the root is past the midpoint and rounds up, so 75≈975​≈9​ inches. To skip the decimal entirely, double both sides and compare 4×75=3004×75=300 with 172=289172=289, which gives the same verdict.
Practice
A ramp rises 4444​ feet. Since 62=3662=36 and 72=4972=49, the height is between 66 and 77. The halfway square is 6.52=42.256.52=42.25. To the nearest whole foot, what is 4444​?
Show the solution
The midpoint between 66 and 77 is 6.56.5, and 6.52=42.256.52=42.25. Since 44>42.2544>42.25, the root is past the midpoint, so 4444​ rounds up and the height is 77​ feet. Doubling first keeps it all in whole numbers, comparing 4×44=1764×44=176 with 132=169132=169.
Practice
A wire is 3131​ inches long. The root is between 5.55.5 and 5.65.6. The halfway square is 5.552=30.80255.552=30.8025. To the nearest tenth, what is 3131​?
Show the solution
The midpoint between 5.55.5 and 5.65.6 is 5.555.55, and 5.552=30.80255.552=30.8025. Since 31>30.802531>30.8025, the root is above 5.555.55 and rounds up, so 31=5.631​=5.6​ to the nearest tenth. Rounding to tenths works exactly like rounding to whole numbers, only the midpoint you square is a halfway tenth.
Practice
A flagpole is 8888​ units tall. The root is between 9.39.3 and 9.49.4. The halfway square is 9.352=87.42259.352=87.4225. To the nearest tenth, what is 8888​?
Show the solution
The midpoint between 9.39.3 and 9.49.4 is 9.359.35, and 9.352=87.42259.352=87.4225. Since 88>87.422588>87.4225, the root is past the midpoint and rounds up, so 88≈9.488​≈9.4​. Comparing 9352=874,2259352=874,225 with 880,000880,000 reaches the same answer using only whole numbers.
Practice
A square field covers 250250 sq yd. Since 152=225152=225 and 162=256162=256, the side 250250​ is between 1515 and 1616. What is the largest whole number less than 250250​?
Show the solution
Since 152=225152=225 and 162=256162=256, we have 225<250<256225<250<256, so 15<250<1615<250​<16. The largest whole number below 250250​ is 1515​.
Practice
A square reservoir has footprint 90009000 sq m. Find the largest whole number less than 90009000​.
Show the solution
Testing squares in the nineties, 942=8836942=8836 and 952=9025952=9025. Since 8836<9000<90258836<9000<9025, the root sits between 9494 and 9595, so the floor is 9494​. When no perfect square is handed to you, size it up first. Here 902=8100902=8100 and 1002=10,0001002=10,000 show the answer is in the nineties.
Practice
Find the largest whole number less than 3,000,0003,000,000​. Since the root is in the seventeen-hundreds, test 1,73221,7322 and 1,73321,7332.
Show the solution
Testing 1,7322=2,999,8241,7322=2,999,824, which is under 3,000,0003,000,000, and 1,7332=3,003,2891,7332=3,003,289, which is over, traps the root between the two. So the largest whole number below 3,000,0003,000,000​ is 17321732​. Only the two squares straddling the target matter, no matter how large the numbers get.
Practice
How many whole numbers nn satisfy 50<n<13050​<n​<130​? Square the bounds and count whole numbers strictly between 5050 and 130130.
Show the solution
Squaring both bounds turns the question into 50<n<13050<n<130, so nn runs from 5151 through 129129. That is 129−51+1=79129−51+1=79​ whole numbers. Both ends are strict, so 5050 and 130130 themselves are left out of the count.
Practice
How many whole numbers kk satisfy 40<k<21040​<k<210​? Find the smallest whole number above 4040​ and the largest below 210210​, then count.
Show the solution
Since 62=36<40<49=7262=36<40<49=72, the smallest whole number above 4040​ is 77. Since 142=196<210<225=152142=196<210<225=152, the largest below 210210​ is 1414. Counting 77 through 1414 gives 14−7+1=814−7+1=8​. Both 77 and 1414 do count here, which is why the run is 88 long and not 77.
Practice
Beam 1 is 7575​ m and Beam 2 is 415415​ m. Square each to compare. Option 1 is Beam 1, Option 2 is Beam 2. Which is longer?
Show the solution
Square each. Beam 1 gives (75)2=49×5=245(75​)2=49×5=245, and Beam 2 gives (415)2=16×15=240(415​)2=16×15=240. Since 245>240245>240 and both lengths are positive, Beam 1 is longer, option 11​.
Practice
Evaluate 363​6. Group the six factors into three pairs. Each pair 3⋅3=33​⋅3​=3. What whole number is the result?
Show the solution
Pair the six factors. Each 323​2 is 33, so 36=(32)3=33=273​6=(3​2)3=33=27​. Any even power of a root comes out a whole number this way, since the copies pair off and each pair leaves the number underneath.
Practice
Two trails are 2828​ miles and 5252​ miles long. What is the largest whole number less than 28+5228​+52​?
Show the solution
Bracket each root with tenths. Since 5.22=27.04<28<28.09=5.325.22=27.04<28<28.09=5.32, we get 5.2<28<5.35.2<28​<5.3, and since 7.22=51.84<52<53.29=7.327.22=51.84<52<53.29=7.32, we get 7.2<52<7.37.2<52​<7.3. Adding the low ends and the high ends separately, the sum lies between 5.2+7.2=12.45.2+7.2=12.4 and 5.3+7.3=12.65.3+7.3=12.6. The largest whole number below the total is 1212​. Whole-number brackets would only give 1212 to 1414, so the tenths are what pin the floor down.
